holidays.name: Eat Outside Day
holidays.description: The unofficial send-off to summer asks you to take your meal out of the kitchen and into the open air. A backyard barbecue counts. So does a park-bench sandwich, a balcony breakfast, or a picnic blanket spread out like a tiny edible kingdom.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It lands on the last day of August, when summer is nearly over, and that timing is probably why it caught on.
holidays.funFact: Many people say food tastes better outdoors. Fresh air and a change of scenery can make a meal feel more memorable, even when it's just a humble sandwich.

holidays.name: National Trail Mix Day
holidays.description: A salute to the snack made of nuts, seeds, dried fruit, and the occasional chocolate candy. Everyone builds it differently, and some people pick out their favorite bits and leave the rest. Mix your own blend and toast the end of summer hiking season.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It was probably created to celebrate a portable snack that suits the final days of summer adventures.
holidays.funFact: Trail mix has a classic nickname, 'gorp'. It's often explained as short for 'good old raisins and peanuts', though the word's exact origin is debated.

holidays.name: National Diatomaceous Earth Day
holidays.description: A distinctly unglamorous holiday honoring a soft, chalky powder made from fossilized microscopic algae. The powder turns up in gardens, filtration systems, and various household and industrial uses. It's a rare chance to celebrate something that is basically ancient sea dust.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It appears to be a niche celebration of a surprisingly versatile natural material.
holidays.funFact: Diatomaceous earth is made of the glassy skeletons of diatoms, single-celled algae that lived in water millions of years ago. Their shells are made of silica.
